ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure there are two intersecting straight lines, A, E, C are on the same straight line, and D, E, B are on the same straight line. The triangle on the left is △ADE, and the triangle on the right is △CBE. The figure marks AD=10, BC=15, BE=6, CE=12, and next to DE is marked 3x−2. At D and B there is each an identical red angle mark, indicating that ∠ADE and ∠CBE are equal; E is the intersection point of the two straight lines. Then reason: Because ∠ADE = ∠CBE, and ∠AED and ∠CEB are vertical angles, therefore ∠AED = ∠CEB. Therefore △ADE ∼ △CBE. The correspondence is A↔C, D↔B, E↔E, so AE corresponds to CE, and AD corresponds to CB. From the similarity ratio, AE/CE = AD/BC = 10/15 = 2/3. Also CE=12, so AE = 12×2/3 = 8.
